questions.question: How did the authors select the split site for the two cat-DHFR rings?

options.A: They chose the α-helix-C/β-sheet-5 boundary at residues 88–89, with GLN +0.726
options.B: They chose the active-site center at residues 23–24 because it had GLN zero
options.C: They selected a structured hydrophobic core site with the lowest linking number
options.D: They split the enzyme at residue 159 to create two equal rings

questions.rationale: The chosen loop-region split preserved the active site and gave highly intertwined segments according to the GLN analysis.
questions.evidence_quote: Combining these criteria, we identified that cleavage at the position between the α-helix-C and β-sheet-5 (residues 88 and 89) would generate two highly intertwined segments (GLN +0.726, Figure S1a ), which could be converted to catenane topology upon cyclization of the two fragments.

questions.question: What chain segments form the two rings, and what GLN did the completed catenane attain?

options.A: Residues 1–88 and 89–159 form the rings; cat-DHFR has GLN +1.120
options.B: Residues 1–23 and 24–159 form the rings; cat-DHFR has GLN +0.726
options.C: Residues 1–89 and 90–159 form the rings; cat-DHFR has GLN −1.120
options.D: Two identical 1–159 chains form rings with GLN zero

questions.rationale: The adopted design divides the enzyme into the two complementary chains and the resulting catenane has greater intertwinement than the virtual split.
questions.evidence_quote: Thus, a design composed of residues 1-88 as one ring and residues 89-159 as the other ring was adopted (Figure 1a ). The two fragments are known to reconstitute efficiently. 42, 45 The entangling core of the design is similar to that of the wild-type and the linker naturally extends to form the ring, giving a cat-DHFR with a GLN of +1.120 (Figure S1b ).

questions.question: Why was ring I circularly permutated to make new termini between residues 23 and 24?

options.A: The two bulky split-intein pairs could interfere, so placing closure motifs on opposite sides improved cyclization geometry
options.B: The active site had to be split between residues 23 and 24 to restore DHFR catalysis
options.C: The permutation shortened the loop to zero residues and increased aggregation
options.D: The termini needed to remain adjacent so both inteins could bind on the same side

questions.rationale: The design accounts for distances between termini and steric interference of the two split-intein pairs.
questions.evidence_quote: Considering that cyclization efficiency depends on the distance between the new termini and that the two bulky split-intein pairs may interfere with each other, ring I was circularly permutated to generate new termini between residues 23 and 24, and the rewired loops were designed to be long enough ( 16residues) to bridge the split structural motifs.

questions.question: What additional element was encoded in the first ring specifically to test the catenane topology?

options.A: A TEV protease recognition sequence whose cleavage should yield one linear and one cyclic fragment
options.B: A fluorescent tag whose emission reports the number of rings
options.C: A His-tag duplicated in both rings to force disulfide formation
options.D: A restriction site designed to cleave the peptide backbone in vitro

questions.rationale: The TEV site enables a topology-sensitive proteolysis assay: cleavage opens one ring but leaves the other cyclic.
questions.evidence_quote: The gene cassette was then designed containing two DHFR segments as the entangling template, two mutually orthogonal split-intein pairs for ring closure, and the tobacco etch virus (TEV) protease recognition sequence in the first ring for subsequent proof of topology by proteolytic digestion experiment

questions.question: What indirect topology test was used after the authors could not obtain suitable cat-DHFR crystals?

options.A: TEV cleavage produced the predicted linear and cyclic fragments, confirmed by SDS-PAGE and LC-MS
options.B: X-ray diffraction resolved both linked rings at atomic resolution
options.C: The protein was reduced to two identical linear fragments by DTT
options.D: Only a far-UV CD spectrum was used to establish mechanical interlocking

questions.rationale: Because crystallography failed, the preinstalled TEV site and the distinct cleavage products provided indirect topology evidence.
questions.evidence_quote: Upon cleavage, cat-DHFR was converted to a linear fragment and a cyclic fragment as expected, which was confirmed by the SDS-PAGE analysis and LC-MS spectra

questions.question: What did the optimized expression and purification reveal about cat-DHFR mobility relative to the linear control?

options.A: At 16 °C for 20 h, cat-DHFR showed a major sub-20-kDa SDS-PAGE band versus about 22 kDa for l-DHFR
options.B: At 37 °C for 2 h, cat-DHFR migrated above 40 kDa versus 20 kDa for l-DHFR
options.C: Cat-DHFR showed no band, while l-DHFR remained soluble only after denaturation
options.D: Both forms had identical mobility and molecular mass above 100 kDa

questions.rationale: The concatenated structure migrates apparently faster in SDS-PAGE, which the authors attribute to its compactness despite unfolded linear chains.
questions.evidence_quote: Protein expression was carried out at 16 o C for 20 h to ensure proper folding and complete reaction. After cell lysis, proteins were purified under native conditions using Ni-NTA affinity chromatography. The eluted products were further purified by size exclusion chromatography (SEC). SDS-PAGE analysis of purified products shows a single band at a molecular weight of approximately 22 kDa for l-DHFR and a major band at less than 20 kDa for cat-DHFR

questions.question: How did cat-DHFR's catalytic rate and substrate affinity compare with the linear control?

options.A: It retained about 5 U/mg versus 14 U/mg, with Km about fivefold higher and kcat about 38%
options.B: It exceeded 14 U/mg, with Km fivefold lower and kcat doubled
options.C: It was inactive, while the linear control was about 5 U/mg
options.D: It had equal activity and identical Km and kcat to the control

questions.rationale: The catenane retains significant but reduced enzyme function, with both substrate affinity and turnover compromised.
questions.evidence_quote: Considering the extensive engineering performed on the structure, it was not surprising at all to see that cat-DHFR has a lower activity (~5 U/mg) than the linear control (~14 U/mg).

questions.question: Which ITC affinity changes most strongly suggest compromised substrate/cofactor binding after concatenation?

options.A: KD increased about 173-fold for DHF and 14-fold for NADPH; THF KD increased about 3.6-fold
options.B: KD decreased 173-fold for DHF and 14-fold for NADPH
options.C: Only THF binding weakened, by 38-fold, while DHF and NADPH were unchanged
options.D: All three ligands bound more tightly by approximately fivefold

questions.rationale: The dissociation constants are larger for cat-DHFR; the largest change is DHF, while product THF also dissociates more readily.
questions.evidence_quote: As shown in Table 1 , the disassociation constants (KD) are generally much larger for cat-DHFR than that for l-DHFR with the corresponding substrates (~173-fold for DHF and ~14-fold for NADPH).

questions.question: What did the DMSO challenge suggest about the catenane's tolerance to a chemical stress?

options.A: At 5% DMSO, cat-DHFR retained 87% activity versus 74% for l-DHFR
options.B: At 5% DMSO, l-DHFR retained 87% while cat-DHFR retained 74%
options.C: Both proteins lost all activity after DMSO exposure
options.D: DMSO increased both proteins' activities above 100%

questions.rationale: The authors interpret greater retained activity for the mechanically interlocked form as enhanced resilience.
questions.evidence_quote: We also tentatively tested the samples' tolerance to organic solvents by adding DMSO to a final concentration of 5% and performing the activity assay. It seems that cat-DHFR has preserved more activity (87%) than l-DHFR (74%)

questions.question: Which caveat constrained the authors' ability to make a direct structural claim about cat-DHFR?

options.A: They did not obtain crystals of sufficient quality and therefore relied on indirect characterization
options.B: The protein could not be expressed in cells
options.C: The LC-MS molecular mass contradicted the proposed composition
options.D: The catenane was insoluble under all native purification conditions

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly say crystallization did not yield suitable crystals, citing possible purity, linker disorder, or substrate-affinity issues.
